title: NWDAF in 5G: Architecture, Use Cases, and Evolution Across 3GPP Releases
authors: Anurag Tiwari; Suvadeep Das; Ajay Kumar; Shikha Srivastava
venue: 2025 National Conference on Communications (NCC)
summary: Overview of the NWDAF covering its architecture, analytics use cases and how its capabilities changed between 3GPP Releases 16 and 17, with a discussion of deployment challenges and open research directions.
method: standards review / survey
key_result: Consolidates the Rel-16/17 NWDAF feature set and use cases and lists research gaps for practical NWDAF deployment.
limitation_or_critique: Short conference overview by C-DOT authors that stops at Rel-17 and has no quantitative evaluation; weaker venue than the existing NWDAF surveys already in the list.

title: Network Digital Twin for 6G and Beyond: An End-to-End View Across Multi-Domain Network Ecosystems
authors: Dinh-Hieu Tran; Nazar Waheed; Yuris Mulya Saputra; Xingqin Lin; Cong T. Nguyen; Tedros Salih Abdu; Van Nhan Vo; Van-Quan Pham; Madyan Alsenwi; Abuzar Babikir Mohammad Adam; Symeon Chatzinotas; Eva Lagunas; Hung Tran; Tu Ho Dac; Nguyen Van Huynh
venue: IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society
summary: Survey of network digital twins for 6G and beyond across RAN, transport, 5G core, cloud/edge, non-terrestrial and quantum networks, with a dedicated treatment of twins of the 5G core.
method: literature survey
key_result: Maps NDT use across network domains from academic and industrial viewpoints and lists open challenges, claiming the first in-depth guide to RAN and core twins.
limitation_or_critique: Very broad scope dilutes the core-network part; as a survey it does not quantify twin fidelity or compare control-plane twin designs experimentally.
standards_link: ITU-T Y.3090; IRTF NMRG NDT draft

title: AI For Core Network in 6G
authors: Reyhan Dede; Nurefşan Ak; Merve Güllü; İbrahim Yazıcı; İsmail Duru
venue: 2025 9th International Symposium on Innovative Approaches in Smart Technologies (ISAS)
summary: Short review of the role of AI in 6G core networks, covering AI-native design, automation and security, and the enablers and requirements of 6G core architectures.
method: literature review / position paper
key_result: Identifies interoperability, energy efficiency, computational cost and standardisation gaps as the main obstacles to AI-native 6G cores.
limitation_or_critique: Broad, qualitative overview in a niche symposium; no systematic method, no evaluation, and little anchoring in specific 3GPP Release 18-20 features.

title: Failures and Resilience in the IP Era: Navigating the Fragility of Modern Telecommunications Networks—The Sovereign Functions
authors: Raymond Owen; Adam Bryant; Leigh Finch; Daniel Franklin; Mahrokh Abdollahi; Mehran Abolhasan
venue: IEEE Access
summary: Failure-centric survey arguing that large telecom outages often originate in shared IP-level functions (routing, naming, time sync) and supporting services (authentication, licensing, configuration) rather than in physical redundancy gaps.
method: survey with real-outage case studies
data_or_testbed: public outage reports and case studies
key_result: Organises real-world outages around interdependent 'sovereign' and supporting functions and derives mitigation directions and their economic consequences.
limitation_or_critique: Qualitative and IP-network-wide; it does not model 5GC NF failover, subscriber-database replication or AI-based assurance.

title: Zero-touch networks: Towards next-generation network automation
authors: Mirna El Rajab; Li Yang; Abdallah Shami
venue: Computer Networks
summary: Surveys zero-touch networks within the ETSI ZSM framework across optimisation, monitoring, energy and security, and adds an AutoML pipeline case study for 5G+ automation.
method: survey plus AutoML pipeline experiment (throughput prediction with drift adaptation)
key_result: Reports that the AutoML pipeline predicts application throughput more accurately than conventionally tuned ML and adapts to data drift.
limitation_or_critique: Broad ZSM survey not specific to the core; the experiment concerns throughput prediction rather than a closed loop acting on core NFs.

title: Assurance and Conflict Detection in Intent-Based Networking: A Comprehensive Survey and Insights on Standards and Open-Source Tools
authors: Molka Gharbaoui; Filippo Sciarrone; Mattia Fontana; Piero Castoldi; Barbara Martini
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Surveys how intent fulfilment is assured and how conflicts between intents are detected across the intent life cycle, with a review of standards and open-source tools.
method: survey
key_result: Organises assurance (AI/ML and monitoring based) and conflict-detection techniques by life-cycle stage and identifies generalisation and scalability as open problems.
limitation_or_critique: Generic IBN scope, not specific to the 5G/6G core or to conflicts between agent-driven loops.
standards_link: TS 28.312; ETSI ZSM 011; IETF/IRTF NMRG intent RFCs

title: Towards Intent-Based Network Management: Large Language Models for Intent Extraction in 5G Core Networks
authors: Dimitrios Michael Manias; Ali Chouman; Abdallah Shami
venue: 2024 20th International Conference on the Design of Reliable Communication Networks (DRCN)
summary: Develops a custom LLM that extracts operator intents for 5G core management as a first step toward end-to-end intent-based networking.
method: fine-tuned LLM for intent extraction
key_result: Shows that a domain-tuned LLM can extract structured intents for core management and outlines integration steps for full intent-based automation.
limitation_or_critique: Stops at intent extraction, without mapping to the TS 28.312 intent model, feasibility checking or a closed loop on live NFs.

title: Improving Traffic Forecasting for 5G Core Network Scalability: A Machine Learning Approach
authors: Imad Alawe; Adlen Ksentini; Yassine Hadjadj-Aoul; Philippe Bertin
venue: IEEE Network
summary: Proposes scaling 5G core VNF resources ahead of demand by forecasting traffic load with neural networks (LSTM and DNN) trained on a real mobile traffic-arrival dataset.
method: LSTM / DNN traffic forecasting driving proactive scaling
key_result: In simulation, forecast-driven scaling reacts faster to load changes and has new resources ready sooner than threshold-based scaling.
limitation_or_critique: Pre-NWDAF work evaluated by simulation only, with a single aggregate load signal and no per-NF or control-plane procedure modelling.
standards_link: TS 23.501 (5GC service-based architecture); ETSI NFV scaling

title: Comparative Analysis of Time Series Prediction Algorithms on Multiple Network Function Data of NWDAF
authors: Dasheng Chen; Qi Song; Yinbin Zhang; Ling Li; Zhiming Yang
venue: International Journal of Distributed Sensor Networks
summary: Releases NWDAF-NFPP, an anonymised dataset of performance time series for eight types of network functions collected in a China Telecom lab, and benchmarks six ML/DL forecasters on it.
method: comparative time-series forecasting (classical ML and deep learning)
data_or_testbed: China Telecom laboratory NF performance data, 5-minute granularity
key_result: Provides one of the few operator-sourced NF-level performance datasets for NWDAF-style load prediction, together with a baseline comparison of six models.
limitation_or_critique: Lab rather than live-network data and a model comparison with no closed-loop use of the forecasts; the abstract does not name the winning model or its margin.

title: Anomaly Detection Employing a 5G Core Data Analytics Framework
authors: Júnia Maísa Oliveira; Jônatan Almeida; Erik De Britto e Silva; Larissa Ferreira Rodrigues Moreira; Rodrigo Moreira; Flávio O. Silva; Daniel F. Macedo; José Marcos Nogueira
venue: 2024 IEEE 13th International Conference on Cloud Networking (CloudNet)
summary: Presents an extensible 5G core data-analytics framework, designed after the 3GPP analytics specifications, that makes it easy to add new analytics scenarios and algorithms to an open-source core lacking an NWDAF.
method: NWDAF-like analytics framework; ML anomaly detection use case
key_result: In a cybersecurity anomaly-detection use case the framework installed easily, accepted new algorithms flexibly and integrated with the core.
limitation_or_critique: Evaluation is qualitative (ease of integration, flexibility) with no reported detection or latency numbers, and new analytics sit outside the standard analytics IDs.

title: Hierarchical Network Data Analytics Framework for 6G Network Automation: Design and Implementation
authors: Youbin Jeon; Sangheon Pack
venue: IEEE Internet Computing
summary: Proposes H-NDAF, a hierarchical NWDAF in which leaf NWDAFs perform inference and a root NWDAF performs training, and applies it to optimising the policy for UE data flows.
method: hierarchical NWDAF (distributed inference, centralised training)
key_result: Leaf-level inference shortens the time to deliver analytics compared with a single NWDAF while keeping accuracy sufficient.
limitation_or_critique: Evaluated on free5GC with simulated load only; the root/leaf split mirrors the Rel-17 MTLF/AnLF separation, but standard model-sharing interfaces and drift handling are not assessed.

title: Residual Artifact Governance With ML-Enabled Garbage Collection Prediction in Kubernetes-Based 5G/6G Service-Based Architecture
authors: Larisa-Mihaela Tufeanu; Marius-Constantin Vochin; Frank Y. Li
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Proposes a master-agent add-on to a Kubernetes-hosted SBA core that learns cleanup policies for leftover cluster objects and predicts when their build-up will destabilise the cluster.
method: ML time-to-collapse prediction plus bounded, periodic fractional garbage collection by per-NF agents
data_or_testbed: Kubernetes-based SBA prototype under nominal and stress leak regimes
key_result: Shows that residual-artifact accumulation can be measured, forecast and kept bounded with Kubernetes-native mechanisms without modifying the core NFs.
limitation_or_critique: Targets a platform-level ageing problem rather than NF or procedure failures, and is validated on a prototype only, without operator workloads.

title: AnomalyTrack: Scalable and Self-Adaptive Anomaly Detection in Large-Scale 5G Networks
authors: Michel Santos Da Silva; Adriano Guilherme Silva Rocha; Lourenco Alves Pereira
venue: 2025 IEEE Symposium on Computers and Communications (ISCC)
summary: Presents a self-adapting KPI anomaly-detection framework for 5G SA networks that combines density-based outlier detectors and seasonal time-series models, and specifies where it runs in the core and what it costs.
method: unsupervised outlier detection (LOF, COF, IF-LOF) plus ARIMA/SARIMA forecasting
data_or_testbed: one year of KPI data from a commercial mobile operator (over half a million KPI series)
key_result: Reports about 97% detection accuracy with inference within a few seconds per 30-minute batch, much faster than the operator's conventional monitoring.
limitation_or_critique: Detection only, on aggregated KPIs; no root-cause localisation, no link to NWDAF/MDA interfaces and no closed-loop action.

title: A Modular, End-to-End Next-Generation Network Testbed: Toward a Fully Automated Network Management Platform
authors: Ali Chouman; Dimitrios Michael Manias; Abdallah Shami
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Describes a modular end-to-end 5G-and-beyond testbed, with RAN integration and real UEs, intended as a platform for analytics-driven and automated network management, and evaluates how faithfully it emulates full network functions from UE registration to user-plane traffic.
method: testbed design and functional evaluation
data_or_testbed: E2E 5G+ testbed (open-source core, RAN, real UEs)
key_result: Shows that the modular testbed reproduces complete control- and user-plane sequences (registration through data sessions) and can host automation experiments; the abstract reports no headline numbers.
limitation_or_critique: Lab-scale infrastructure paper: it enables, but does not itself evaluate, NWDAF analytics or closed loops, and has no fault or load campaigns.

title: Smart Scaling of the 5G Core Network: An RNN-Based Approach
authors: Imad Alawe; Yassine Hadjadj-Aoul; Adlen Ksentini; Philippe Bertin; Cesar Viho; Davy Darche
venue: 2018 IEEE Global Communications Conference (GLOBECOM)
summary: Uses recurrent neural networks to predict upcoming control- and data-plane load of a virtualised 5G core and schedules scale-out and scale-in ahead of demand.
method: RNN load forecasting with proactive provisioning schedule
data_or_testbed: discrete-event simulation with an operator traffic trace
key_result: The forecast-based scaler is reported to be more robust than threshold-based scaling in keeping QoS during load increases.
limitation_or_critique: Simulation-only evaluation that treats the core as a generic VNF pool, without real NF implementations or failure scenarios.

title: From Detection to Policy: Calibrated and Explainable Closed-Loop DDoS Management in 5G/B5G Networks
authors: Shihab Hasan; Tarek R. Sheltami; Ashraf S. Mahmoud
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Turns NWDAF-style DDoS detection into graduated mitigation by calibrating classifier confidence and scoring attack severity from SHAP contributions, then choosing terminate, throttle or monitor.
method: isotonic-regression calibration, SHAP-based severity score, threshold-optimised policy
key_result: Keeps high threat coverage while almost eliminating terminations of benign users, unlike deep-learning baselines, and lowers expected calibration error.
limitation_or_critique: Offline evaluation on a public dataset; the actions are not enforced through standard actuators (e.g. PCF/SMF) inside a running core.

title: AI as a Service for Intelligent Mobile Networks: Extending Network Data Analytics Functions
authors: Carlos Barroso-Fernández; Adam Zahir; Pablo Picazo-Martínez; Antonio de la Oliva; Carlos J. Bernardos
venue: IEEE Communications Standards Magazine
summary: Designs an AI-as-a-Service platform inside the 5G core whose distributed AI workers partly reuse the NWDAF and whose central control layer orchestrates services, so that NFs and UEs can consume AI models in the network.
method: platform architecture and proof-of-concept implementation
key_result: The proof of concept shows AIaaS can run within a realistic 5G deployment for both internal and external consumers; the abstract gives no quantitative figures.
limitation_or_critique: Feasibility-level PoC without reported latency, energy or scaling numbers, and the extensions beyond the NWDAF service model are not yet standardised.

title: Intelligence Enhancement of NWDAF on Vertical Federated Learning towards Next Generation Core Network
authors: Meiyu Yin; Zhen Li; Song Zhao; Jinyan Li; Heng Wang
venue: 2026 International Wireless Communications and Mobile Computing (IWCMC)
summary: Proposes an NWDAF capability-management framework for vertical federated learning, with management procedures for the different VFL server roles and configuration mechanisms for the full VFL life cycle.
method: architecture and procedure design
key_result: Defines the management procedures and configuration needed to orchestrate VFL among NWDAFs across domains; the abstract reports no quantitative results.
limitation_or_critique: Design-level proposal from China Telecom researchers with no evaluation reported in the abstract, so the Rel-19 VFL feature remains unevaluated in practice.

title: SCOPE-5G: A Standards-Aligned Synthetic AMF Observability Dataset for Reproducible 5G Core Benchmarking
authors: Silvio R. Araujo; Carlos A. Kamienski; Reinaldo A. C. Bianchi
venue: IEEE Access
summary: Introduces SCOPE-5G, an open framework and synthetic dataset of AMF observability data aligned with 3GPP performance-measurement definitions and seeded with labelled gradual-onset anomalies for benchmarking 5G-core methods.
method: synthetic data generation (queueing, diurnal and long-range-dependent load models, sigmoid anomaly injection)
data_or_testbed: synthetic AMF dataset: 21 procedures, 3 slices, 60 days at 15-min granularity; validated against public references incl. Telecom Italia CDR
key_result: Statistical checks against public references show close agreement (Pearson r about 0.98 with Telecom Italia CDR), and replacing gradual with step anomalies raises detection AUC from 0.919 to 0.998, showing step faults overstate detector quality.
limitation_or_critique: Synthetic data at 15-minute granularity that the authors admit cannot replace operator telemetry; AMF-only, with no SBI/SCP-level traces or UE-level procedure outcomes.

title: Autonomic Closed-Loop Service Management based on Interworking Multiple AI Models
authors: Takahiro Hirayama-; Masahiro Jibiki; Takuya Miyasaka; Minato Sakuraba; Junichi Kawasaki; Satoshi Akabori; Takayuki Kuroda
venue: NOMS 2025-2025 IEEE Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Defines a unified interface through which several AI models (self-monitoring, self-configuration, self-optimisation) cooperate to run closed-loop management of cloud-native network functions, including reacting to predicted failures.
method: interworking of three AI models in an autonomic closed loop with failure prediction
key_result: The prototype builds network services automatically and keeps the QoS of running services by acting on past and predicted failure events.
limitation_or_critique: Prototype description with little quantitative evaluation; not mapped to 3GPP actuators such as NF reselection or TS 23.527 restoration.
standards_link: ETSI ZSM 009 (closed loops); TS 28.535/28.536 (assurance closed loop)

title: A Decentralized Collaborative Learning Approach in 5G+ Core Networks
authors: Mohammad Arif Hossain; Abdullah Ridwan Hossain; Weiqi Liu; Nirwan Ansari; Abbas Kiani; Tony Saboorian
venue: IEEE Network
summary: Proposes two distributed NWDAF training architectures for the 5G+ core: federated learning across NF instances, and split learning that partitions the model between entities.
method: federated and split learning across NF instances
key_result: Argues that both variants improve data locality, security, training overhead and time, and accuracy compared with centralised NWDAF training; the abstract gives no figures.
limitation_or_critique: Magazine-style article with no quantitative results in the abstract; split learning is not part of the 3GPP NWDAF FL procedures.

title: Evaluating CAP Theorem on a Stateless 5G Core
authors: Siddhesh Pratim Sovitkar; Shwetha Vittal; Antony Franklin A
venue: 2024 IEEE 21st Consumer Communications & Networking Conference (CCNC)
summary: Measures the consistency-versus-availability trade-off of a 3GPP-compliant stateless 5GC whose NFs share an external state store, running it in CP and AP modes under network partition.
method: testbed experiments comparing CP and AP operating modes of the shared state store
key_result: CP mode completes more PDU session establishments correctly but is less available than AP mode, quantifying the CAP trade-off for core state.
limitation_or_critique: Short paper on a single site; it does not consider cross-site (geo-redundant) replication, failover time or the effect on UE retries.

title: 5GC-Analyser: Demistifying the 5G Core Network Through Statistical Analysis
authors: Abderaouf Khichane; Ilhem Fajjari; Nadjib Aitsaadi; Mourad Gueroui
venue: ICC 2024 - IEEE International Conference on Communications
summary: Statistically analyses dependencies and causal links among the metrics of 5GC microservices to decide which observability techniques suit online monitoring of the core.
method: statistical correlation and causality analysis of NF/microservice metrics
data_or_testbed: cloud-native 5GC with simulated users replaying conditions observed on an operator's (Orange) gNBs
key_result: Reveals inter-NF metric dependencies that inform the choice of online observability and proactive degradation detection methods.
limitation_or_critique: Exploratory analysis without a deployed detector or RCA benchmark; the results are a basis for later work rather than a closed loop.

title: Digital Twins for 5G Networks: A Modeling and Deployment Methodology
authors: Mario Sanz Rodrigo; Diego Rivera; José Ignacio Moreno; Manuel Àlvarez-Campana; Diego R. López
venue: IEEE Access
summary: Proposes a methodology and architecture to build and operate a mobile-network digital twin of a 5G core environment, covering data acquisition, modelling, use and the bidirectional link to the physical network (B5GEMINI project).
method: NDT design methodology and reference architecture
key_result: Defines an end-to-end life cycle for automatically creating and using a 5G-core digital twin, applied to cybersecurity and Industry 4.0 scenarios.
limitation_or_critique: Methodological contribution; the abstract reports no measured twin fidelity and no prediction of control-plane action outcomes.

title: Failure-Aware and Automated Disaster Backup in the 5G Core Network
authors: Huahong Zhu; Jianzhao Li; Jianyuan Hu; Wenyun Li
venue: 2022 International Communication Engineering and Cloud Computing Conference (CECCC)
summary: Uses NWDAF failure detection to trigger an automated disaster backup in which the 4G HSS takes over from the 5G UDM when all UDM instances fail.
method: analytics-triggered failover procedure; fault-tree and probabilistic reliability analysis
key_result: Fault-tree and probability analysis indicate higher subscriber-data availability without adding redundant UDM capacity.
limitation_or_critique: Evaluated analytically only, in a weak venue, with no UE-procedure-level measurements or cross-site UDR replication.

title: LOCOMOTIVE 5G Core for 6G ready Resilient and Highly Available Network Slices and SFCs
authors: Sourav Sarkar; Shwetha Vittal; Antony Franklin A
venue: 2022 18th International Conference on Network and Service Management (CNSM)
summary: Designs a resilient load-balancing layer for the 5GC control plane, built with XDP/eBPF, and compares it with classic hot-standby redundancy under overload and load-balancer failure.
method: eBPF/XDP-based load balancer with active-active redundancy
key_result: Serves at least 16% more control-plane requests under overload, drops 22% fewer during load-balancer failure and gains about 4% availability over hot standby.
limitation_or_critique: Single-site evaluation focused on the load balancer; no learning component and no cross-site or database failover.

title: A Feasibility Study Toward Trustworthy 3GPP NWDAF Closed-Loop Analytics via Distributed MTLF with OpenDaisy
authors: Ted T. Kuo; Tsung-Han Chang; Li-Jen Wang
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Communications Workshops (ICC Workshops)
summary: Feasibility study of NWDAF closed-loop analytics in which the MTLF is implemented as hierarchical federated learning across sites and stressed with controlled traffic regime shifts and non-IID data (OpenDaisy).
method: hierarchical federated learning as distributed MTLF; drift detection and retraining
key_result: Deployed models failed badly under drift (error 52.1% above an AR(1) baseline), and federated retraining cut regime error by 35% and worst-case error by up to 60%.
limitation_or_critique: Workshop paper with controlled synthetic regime shifts; severe heterogeneity triples outcome variance, and actuation from the retrained analytics is not shown.

title: Knowledge Graph-Based Propagation for Failure Localization in 5G Core Networks
authors: Abubakar Isah; Ibrahim Aliyu; Seungmin Oh; Jaehyung Park; Minsoo Hahn; Jinsul Kim
venue: 2026 Seventeenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
summary: Localises failures in the 5G core by building a failure knowledge graph of NFs, telemetry features and KPIs, compared through a data-driven graph-attention propagation model and a protocol-aware knowledge-driven reasoning model.
method: knowledge graph + relation-aware graph attention; knowledge-guided hierarchical reasoning
data_or_testbed: real-world 5G core telemetry (operator not named in abstract)
key_result: Both paradigms improve localisation accuracy and robustness, with the learned model stronger on prediction and the knowledge-driven one on interpretability.
limitation_or_critique: Short conference paper; the abstract gives no numbers or dataset details, and failure localisation is not linked to a remediation action.

title: A Dynamic UPF Fault Recovery Mechanism for Enhanced Resilience in 5G Core Networks
authors: Shirin Behnaminia; Pardis Yavari; Zeinab Zali; Mohammad Reza Heidarpour
venue: arXiv preprint
summary: Adds UPF failure detection, application-layer PDU session restoration and failure-history-aware UPF selection to an OpenAirInterface core.
method: heartbeat-based failure detection, session restoration, failure-aware UPF selection
data_or_testbed: OpenAirInterface 5GC with TCP and UDP traffic
key_result: Restores connectivity within a few seconds after a UPF failure with low packet loss.
limitation_or_critique: Recent preprint, single-site lab; not compared with standard SMF-driven PFCP restoration in TS 23.527.

title: Demonstrating Per-UE Energy Consumption Monitoring Using Energy Information Function
authors: Federico Tonini; Gaetano Francesco Pittalà; Giovanni Preziosi; Davide Borsatti; Wint Yi Poe; Riccardo Trivisonno; Walter Cerroni
venue: NOMS 2026-2026 IEEE Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Demonstrates an end-to-end, 3GPP-aligned energy measurement chain in which an extended Energy Information Function exposes per-UE energy consumption to an Application Function.
method: prototype of the Rel-19 EIF with exposure to an AF that adapts IoT algorithms and data streams
key_result: Shows (qualitatively, as a demo) that an AF can monitor per-UE energy through the EIF and adapt its service behaviour accordingly.
limitation_or_critique: A short demo paper covering user-plane/IoT energy attribution only, with no control-plane NF energy or energy-aware NF selection.

title: Agentic GitOps: Multi-Step Operational Coordination for Intent-Driven 5G Networks
authors: Phuong Bac Ta; Mafeni Vitumbiko; Duc Thong Thai Nguyen; Younghan Kim
venue: NOMS 2026-2026 IEEE Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Combines an LLM agent layer with declarative GitOps actuation, so that intents become verifiable commits coordinating multi-step reconfiguration of cloud-native 5G NFs via an MCP interface.
method: LLM agent + Model Context Protocol + GitOps desired-state reconciliation
key_result: Reaches a 78% success rate even with goal-only intents while cutting pre-encoded controller logic from 18 to 8 resolution steps.
limitation_or_critique: A single reconfiguration case study; failure modes of the remaining 22% and the latency against core timing budgets are not characterised.

title: Type-Safe Decision Frameworks for Agentic 5G Control: A Theory-Driven Testbed Characterization of Where They Can Be Applied
authors: Michail-Alexandros Kourtis; George Xilouris
venue: arXiv preprint
summary: Characterises when agentic controllers of a 5G core can be trusted if every decision must come from a declared option set, using checkable predicates for timeliness, type conformance, certification cost and cardinality.
method: three typed-decision designs (hosted typed model, fine-tuned typed encoder, retrofitted LLM) with an act/escalate/abstain gate and conformal risk control
data_or_testbed: Open5GS/UERANSIM testbed with a closed core-policy loop
key_result: The fine-tuned typed encoder repeated its training answer for 98-99.5% of changed questions and its gate then acted wrongly on up to 80% of them, versus at most about 14% for the question-reading designs, which were slower or needed an 8B model.
limitation_or_critique: Recent single-group preprint on a small lab core; the decision classes are policy-loop choices rather than full multi-NF remediation.

title: Digital Twin For 5G Networks and Beyond: Domain Transfer and Network Behavior Classification for 6G Readiness
authors: Matej Petrík; David Truhlář; Michal Ries
venue: 2025 International Symposium ELMAR
summary: Builds an open-source digital twin of a 5G network (Open5GS and UERANSIM) that monitors core-network metrics in real time and classifies traffic behaviour with LSTMs trained on twin-generated data.
method: LSTM classification trained in the twin, tested on simulated and real traffic
data_or_testbed: Open5GS + UERANSIM twin; real network traffic for testing
key_result: The twin runs in real time and supports online fine-tuning, but models trained on twin data lose much accuracy on real traffic, exposing a sim-to-real fidelity gap.
limitation_or_critique: Regional conference with a small setup; the accuracy drop is reported qualitatively in the abstract and no domain-adaptation remedy is evaluated.

title: A Scalable and Fault-Tolerant 5G Core on Kubernetes
authors: Sourav Paul; Tanvi Keluskar; Mythili Vutukuru
venue: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
summary: Starts from a production-grade 3GPP-compliant core and builds several cloud-native variants that use Kubernetes failover and auto-scaling differently, then compares their scalability and resilience.
method: design-space comparison of cloud-native 5GC variants on Kubernetes
key_result: Exposes measurable trade-offs between performance, fault tolerance and cloud overhead, with guidance on which design choices to adopt.
limitation_or_critique: Single-cluster study; geo-redundant sites, subscriber-database failover and AI-driven decisions are outside its scope.

title: ForenSiX: Automated Network Forensics and Diagnostics for Beyond-5G and 6G Networks Using Large Language Models
authors: Xuanbo Huang; Kaiping Xue; Lutong Chen; Jiangping Han; Jian Li; David S. L. Wei
venue: IEEE Network
summary: Combines a data-dependency graph derived statically from standards, NF source code and configuration with LLM-assisted log tracking to locate root causes of subscriber-visible failures across core NFs.
method: static dependency-graph construction plus regex and off-the-shelf LLM log analysis
key_result: Demonstrates automated tracing of faults across multiple NFs in realistic scenarios with good reliability and adaptability (qualitative in the abstract).
limitation_or_critique: Magazine-style evaluation on an open-source lab; no public benchmark, accuracy against baselines or LLM error analysis is reported in the abstract.

title: Proactive 5G Core Network Failure Prediction using Nonlinear Dynamical Analysis and Statistical Outlier Detection
authors: Pragadeeswari Selvakumar; Marius Corici; Arun Prakash; Marcus Purat
venue: 2025 IEEE Globecom Workshops (GC Wkshps)
summary: Studies the dynamics of 5GC control-plane metrics with phase-space reconstruction and, finding no chaos, predicts failures by tracking the density of Mahalanobis-distance outliers.
method: Takens embedding and Lyapunov analysis, then hypersphere/Mahalanobis outlier-density thresholding
data_or_testbed: control-plane metrics from a 5G core testbed
key_result: Rising outlier density is a lightweight early-warning signal of failure risk, suitable for real-time use (no accuracy figure in the abstract).
limitation_or_critique: Workshop paper with threshold-based alarms; no localisation of the faulty NF and no comparison with learned detectors.

title: The Agentic-AI Core: An AI-Empowered, Mission-Oriented Core Network for Next-Generation Mobile Telecommunications
authors: Xu Li; Weisen Shi; Hang Zhang; Chenghui Peng; Shaoyun Wu; Wen Tong
venue: Engineering
summary: Proposes a mission-oriented 6G core in which autonomous network agents turn natural-language customer intents into workflows of network capabilities using a large network AI model.
method: architecture proposal: agents plus a telecom-tuned large network model composing capability workflows
key_result: Argues, through two use cases, that agent-composed workflows could make the core more agile and shorten standardisation cycles.
limitation_or_critique: Industrial vision with no quantitative evaluation of reliability, latency or safety of agent-generated procedures.

title: A-Core: A Novel Framework of Agentic AI in the 6G Core Network
authors: Wen Tong; Wei Huo; Thierry Lejkin; Joel Penhoat; Chenghui Peng; Carlos Pereira; Fei Wang; Shaoyun Wu; Lu Yang; Yuanming Shi
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Communications Workshops (ICC Workshops)
summary: Introduces A-Core, a framework that couples a network-wide core large model, generative network instances and role-specialised GenAI agents to create customised services in a 6G core.
method: multi-agent GenAI architecture with a core-network large model
key_result: A case study suggests (qualitatively) faster service creation, and the paper lists design and implementation issues for agentic cores.
limitation_or_critique: Workshop-level concept paper without measured results, safety mechanisms or alignment with 3GPP NF procedures.

title: Design of an AI-driven Network Digital Twin for advanced 5G-6G network management
authors: Amit Karamchandani; Mario Sanz; Ángela Burgaleta; Luis De La Cal; Alberto Mozo; Jose Ignacio Moreno; Antonio Pastor; Diego R. López
venue: NOMS 2024-2024 IEEE Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Describes the architecture, infrastructure and AI use cases of the B5GEMINI network digital twin for 5G-6G management, with a detailed case of ML-based detection of a DNS-over-HTTPS denial-of-service attack inside a 5G network.
method: NDT architecture + ML attack detection use case
data_or_testbed: B5GEMINI-INFRA emulated 5G network with on-demand traffic generation
key_result: Demonstrates that the twin supports isolated, repeatable experiments for generating training data and comparing detection and mitigation tools without touching the live network.
limitation_or_critique: Focus is security experimentation; the twin is an emulation sandbox, not a synchronised replica, and no what-if prediction of operational actions is evaluated.

title: Congestion Control by Mobile Core and RAN Coordination in 5G Mobile Network
authors: Takuya Kato; Takuya Miyasaka; Atsushi Tagami
venue: 2023 IEEE 97th Vehicular Technology Conference (VTC2023-Spring)
summary: Addresses the reconnection storm after large-scale failures by letting an orchestration platform, rather than an overloaded AMF, compute traffic-reduction rates applied at base stations.
method: RAN-core coordinated congestion control computed by the orchestrator
key_result: Recovery converges within about 9% of the theoretical limit, and the paper lists gaps in 3GPP and O-RAN specifications for implementing the scheme.
limitation_or_critique: Simulation-only; UE behaviour is modelled at aggregate level, without NAS timers or per-procedure outcomes.
standards_link: TS 23.501 (AMF overload control); TS 24.501 (NAS back-off); O-RAN

title: B5GEMINI: AI-Driven Network Digital Twin
authors: Alberto Mozo; Amit Karamchandani; Sandra Gómez-Canaval; Mario Sanz; Jose Ignacio Moreno; Antonio Pastor
venue: Sensors
summary: Journal presentation of B5GEMINI, an AI-driven network digital twin for 5G and beyond, describing its infrastructure, its AI ecosystem and two ML use cases.
method: NDT platform design + ML use cases
key_result: Shows the twin being used to design ML-based attack detectors and to develop energy-efficient ML components via a modular Digital Map concept.
limitation_or_critique: Platform and use-case description; twin fidelity against the physical network and control-plane procedure behaviour are not quantified (journal companion of the NOMS 2022 seed).

title: Admission Control for 5G Core Network Slicing Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: William F. Villota-Jacome; Oscar Mauricio Caicedo Rendon; Nelson L. S. da Fonseca
venue: IEEE Systems Journal
summary: Proposes RL (SARA) and deep RL (DSARA) mechanisms for admission control and resource allocation of network slices in the 5G core, distinguishing core and edge nodes and batching requests in time windows.
method: Q-learning and DQN-based admission control
key_result: Both mechanisms outperform existing admission-control schemes for core-network slicing in provider profit and resource utilisation.
limitation_or_critique: Simulation-based and abstracts the core as compute nodes; no NF-level or 3GPP slice-admission (NSACF) modelling and no safety mechanism for the RL policy.

title: Mobility Prediction for 5G Core Networks
authors: Jaeseong Jeong; Dinand Roeland; Jesper Derehag; Ake Ai Johansson; Venkatesh Umaashankar; Gordon Sun; Goran Eriksson
venue: IEEE Communications Standards Magazine
summary: Ericsson authors give a taxonomy of mobility-prediction frameworks for the 5G core, from data collection to model serving within the 3GPP analytics architecture, and evaluate two use cases on live-network data.
method: taxonomy plus ML mobility prediction (e.g. ML-assisted adaptive paging)
key_result: ML-assisted adaptive paging reduced paging signalling overhead by up to 75%.
limitation_or_critique: Magazine article focused on mobility use cases; model life cycle, drift and integration with NWDAF service interfaces are only sketched.

title: AI-Driven Provisioning in the 5G Core
authors: Amit Sheoran; Sonia Fahmy; Lianjie Cao; Puneet Sharma
venue: IEEE Internet Computing
summary: Discusses how orchestrators should place and scale 5G core functions per network slice to meet slice SLOs on shared infrastructure, and argues for AI-driven, functionality-aware placement and scaling.
method: position/design article with AI-driven scaling coupled to NF-aware placement
data_or_testbed: illustrative evaluation (no public dataset reported in the abstract)
key_result: Argues qualitatively that coupling learned scaling with awareness of each core function's role lets providers meet per-slice SLOs with fewer resources.
limitation_or_critique: Magazine-style article whose evidence is illustrative rather than a systematic evaluation on a real core.

title: A Feasibility-Shielded Agentic AI Framework for 6G Self-Healing Core Networks
authors: Yen-Ting Chen; Tuck Wai Choong; Yu-Chiao Jhuang; Jenq-Shiou Leu
venue: 2026 Joint European Conference on Networks and Communications & 6G Summit (EuCNC/6G Summit)
summary: Proposes a cognitive-digital-twin agent for fault remediation in a 6G core whose LLM-proposed actions pass a deterministic feasibility shield and a short-horizon lookahead simulation before execution.
method: LLM agent on an OODA loop + knowledge base + deterministic feasibility shield + lookahead simulation of candidate actions
data_or_testbed: 3GPP-compliant 6G core simulator with injected link failures
key_result: Improves packet delivery ratio by about 39 percentage points during critical link failures over a no-intervention baseline.
limitation_or_critique: Simulator-only study against a weak no-action baseline, and the faults are link failures rather than NF or database failures.
found_via: manual (Crossref title search while recovering Ameur2026Agenticsurvey references; not a citation link)

title: Digital Twin for 5G and Beyond
authors: Huan X. Nguyen; Ramona Trestian; Duc To; Mallik Tatipamula
venue: IEEE Communications Magazine
summary: Magazine-style position paper arguing that digital twins, borrowed from manufacturing and other industries, can support the design, deployment and operation of 5G and beyond networks.
method: conceptual analysis / vision
key_result: Frames the network digital twin as an AI-assisted tool for planning and operating 5G and outlines its expected benefits and open challenges, without quantitative results.
limitation_or_critique: Early vision article with no implementation, no fidelity metric and no specific treatment of the core control plane.

title: Monarch: Monitoring Architecture for 5G and Beyond Network Slices
authors: Niloy Saha; Nashid Shahriar; Muhammad Sulaiman; Noura Limam; Raouf Boutaba; Aladdin Saleh
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Monarch is a cloud-native monitoring architecture that computes per-slice and per-NF KPIs end-to-end and adapts monitoring granularity and collection rates for each slice.
method: scalable monitoring pipeline with adaptive (heuristic) KPI collection
data_or_testbed: 5G slice testbed with up to 50 slices; real-world 5G dataset
key_result: Ingestion time stayed at about 2.25-2.75 ms as the number of slices grew, and adaptive monitoring cut monitoring overhead by up to 76% with acceptable accuracy.
limitation_or_critique: A data-collection substrate rather than an analytics producer: it does not follow the 3GPP DCCF/ADRF data-collection services and uses a simple heuristic for adaptation.
standards_link: cf. TS 23.288 data collection (DCCF/ADRF); TS 28.554 slice KPIs

title: Dual Self-Attention is What You Need for Model Drift Detection in 6G Networks
authors: Mazene Ameur; Bouziane Brik; Adlen Ksentini
venue: IEEE Transactions on Machine Learning in Communications and Networking
summary: Detects data, label and concept drift in telecom ML models with a dual self-attention autoencoder that monitors inputs and targets and captures feature and temporal fluctuations.
method: autoencoder with feature and temporal self-attention
data_or_testbed: three telecom datasets (two time-series, one not)
key_result: Improved drift-detection accuracy by more than 13.6% and cut detection latency by 94.7% compared with state-of-the-art detectors.
limitation_or_critique: Generic 6G drift detector evaluated offline; not tied to NWDAF accuracy monitoring or MTLF retraining triggers.
standards_link: cf. TS 23.288 Rel-18 ML model accuracy monitoring

title: PP5GS—An Efficient Procedure-Based and Stateless Architecture for Next-Generation Core Networks
authors: Endri Goshi; Raffael Stahl; Hasanin Harkous; Mu He; Rastin Pries; Wolfgang Kellerer
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Re-decomposes the 5GC into stateless per-procedure NFs that keep UE context externally, to cut inter-NF signalling and simplify orchestration.
method: procedure-based functional decomposition with external state; Kubernetes deployment
data_or_testbed: private cloud orchestrated with Kubernetes, four control-plane procedures
key_result: Uses up to 34-55% less compute than stateful and stateless baselines, at least 40% less signalling, and completes complex procedures up to 50% faster.
limitation_or_critique: Evaluates efficiency and latency, not failover time or behaviour when the shared state store fails or is replicated across sites.

title: Estimating 5G Network Service Resilience Against Short Timescale Traffic Variation
authors: Rui Li; Bertrand Decocq; Anne Barros; Yi-Ping Fang; Zhiguo Zeng
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Builds a model of a virtualised 5G network that couples traffic dynamics with management mechanisms such as auto-scaling, to estimate how resilient each service is to short bursts of abnormal traffic.
method: analytical/simulation resilience model of traffic variation and management reactions
key_result: Quantifies service-level resilience under traffic surges and compares auto-scaling and isolation strategies, offering guidance for deployment and configuration.
limitation_or_critique: Simulation-only and focused on traffic surges; it does not cover NF or database failures or validate the model against a running core.

title: Centralized and Federated Learning for Predictive VNF Autoscaling in Multi-Domain 5G Networks and Beyond
authors: Tejas Subramanya; Roberto Riggio
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Frames horizontal and vertical VNF autoscaling as forecasting the needed instance count from expected traffic, and compares centralised with federated deep-learning models across administrative domains.
method: deep-learning time-series forecasting; federated vs centralised training; Kubernetes orchestration prototype
key_result: Federated models give forecasting quality close to centralised ones while keeping domain data local, and the forecasts drive a working Kubernetes autoscaler.
limitation_or_critique: Targets generic MEC VNFs rather than 5G core control-plane NFs, and scaling quality is judged mostly by forecast error rather than end-to-end procedure KPIs.

title: Digital Twin-Accelerated Online Deep Reinforcement Learning for Admission Control in Sliced Communication Networks
authors: Zhenyu Tao; Wei Xu; Xiaohu You
venue: IEEE Transactions on Communications
summary: Combines a behaviour-cloning digital twin of a sliced network's admission policy with online deep reinforcement learning so the agent starts from a safe default policy and converges faster in the real network.
method: DT (neural behaviour cloning) + online DRL
data_or_testbed: simulation of a sliced queueing network
key_result: The twin-accelerated online DRL is more stable and converges faster, improving resource utilisation by up to 26.39% over a state-of-the-art DRL baseline while matching long-term revenue.
limitation_or_critique: Simulation-only and focused on slice admission rather than core NF operations; the twin mimics the policy, not the network, so it cannot predict outcomes of new actions.

title: Building Network Digital Twins Part I: State Synchronization
authors: John Sengendo; Fabrizio Granelli
venue: 2024 3rd International Conference on 6G Networking (6GNet)
summary: Analyses the delay chain of state synchronisation between a physical network and its digital twin and proposes prediction-based 'negative delay' to keep the twin in near real-time sync.
method: analytical delay-chain model + predictive synchronisation
key_result: Argues that predicting the physical state can offset acquisition, modelling and transmission delays, enabling near real-time twin synchronisation.
limitation_or_critique: Conceptual and generic (not core-specific); synchronisation accuracy is a fidelity proxy but no end-to-end twin fidelity metric is reported.

title: Enabling simulation services for digital twins of 5G/B5G mobile networks
authors: Giovanni Nardini; Giovanni Stea
venue: Computer Communications
summary: Argues that a digital twin of a 5G/B5G mobile network should offer discrete-event simulation services for what-if analysis, and presents a framework built on Simu5G with lockstep and branching analysis modes.
method: DES-based twin framework (Simu5G/OMNeT++)
key_result: Defines lockstep and branching what-if analysis so the twin can anticipate the effect of faults and reconfigurations before they are applied.
limitation_or_critique: Radio-access oriented simulator; core control-plane procedures and the speed of the what-if loop relative to control-plane timescales are not addressed.

title: Digital Twin Driven Service Self-Healing With Graph Neural Networks in 6G Edge Networks
authors: Peng Yu; Junye Zhang; Honglin Fang; Wenjing Li; Lei Feng; Fanqin Zhou; Pei Xiao; Song Guo
venue: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications
summary: Proposes a digital-twin-based service self-healing mechanism for 6G edge networks that uses GNN performance prediction to detect abnormal links and nodes and to redeploy services away from them.
method: DT + GNN delay prediction + GNN-assisted service redeployment
key_result: The GNN twin predicts flow-level delays accurately, flags abnormal elements, and its redeployment lowers service delay and improves load balance.
limitation_or_critique: Edge/IP-level services rather than 5G core NFs; the twin evaluates redeployment but is not tied to standard NF selection or restoration mechanisms.

title: Enabling emerging edge applications through a 5G control plane intervention
authors: Mukhtiar Ahmad; Muhammad Ali Nawazish; Muhammad Taimoor Tariq; Muhammad Basit Iqbal Awan; Muhammad Taqi Raza; Zafar Ayyub Qazi
venue: Proceedings of the 18th International Conference on emerging Networking EXperiments and Technologies
summary: Proposes CellClone, an edge-based control plane that runs several active clones of control-plane functions with a quorum consistency protocol to mask faults and stragglers.
method: active replication with a custom low-latency quorum consistency protocol
data_or_testbed: testbed replaying real cellular control traces
key_result: Speeds up control-plane operations by a median of over 3.8x under node failures and stragglers and cuts missed application deadlines by over 90%.
limitation_or_critique: Redesigns the control plane rather than using 3GPP restoration; replication cost and geo-distributed deployment are not evaluated against standard UDSF-based designs.
